subject: MedSentryX: Strategic flex credit approval request — POC → Enterprise path
messages:
From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwoodinference.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: 
Date: 2028-04-10T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: MedSentryX — request for flex credit exception (POC → enterprise)

Hi team,

Quick context: MedSentryX (regional health-tech prospect) wants to convert a 3-month POC into a multi-year enterprise commitment but procurement has a hard procurement cadence that forces a start-of-fiscal Q2 commitment. They asked for a blended effective rate that sits ~28% below our published starter slab for the first 12 months to make the economics work for their board.

Why this matters:
- The account has a strong strategic signal (clinical workflows + potential platform embed across 6 hospitals).
- Procurement timeline means we either accept an above-policy commercial structure now or risk losing the deal until Q4.
- Estimated ARR if converted = $1.1M in year one; multiyear ARR expansion potential + references.

What I'm asking:
1) Approval for a one-time "flex credit" of up to 28% off the starter slab for the first 12 months, amortized as a committed credit (not a retro rebate).
2) Permission to include a clause capping the credit to the first $300k consumption; after that normal rates apply.
3) Exec signoff (VP/CFO) — finance wants a memo that documents cadence, precedent, and P&L impact.

I've attached: MedSentryX_MA_plan.xlsx (commercials + forecast), redwood_flex_credit_matrix.pdf (how this maps to our exceptions grid), procurement timeline .msg.

Proposed fallback if signoff not granted: Offer a two-step onramp (40% credit for POC month, 15% for months 2–6) — lower upside for Redwood and likely less convincing for procurement.

Happy to hop on a quick 20-minute call if you want to walk numbers.

Thanks,
Priyom
Account Executive — Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
+1 (415) 555-0198

Attachment stubs: MedSentryX_MA_plan.xlsx (spreadsheet), redwood_flex_credit_matrix.pdf (pdf), MedSentryX_procurement_timeline.msg (email file)

Priyom — thanks for the write-up and the attachments. Quick questions before I posture to finance modeling:

1) How certain is the 12-month consumption profile in the spreadsheet? Is the $1.1M ARR conservative or optimistic? Please confirm which line items are committed vs. expected.
2) Is the proposed "cap at $300k" negotiable (we should aim to limit downside if consumption spikes).
3) Any precedent for a blended effective rate at this depth? If not, flag the closest examples and outcomes.

I can draft a short memo for Markus' review but need the answers above and a simple sensitivity table (cases: conservative/expected/upside) showing EBITDA impact for the first 12 months. Can you get that to me by EOD 4/12?

-Laura
Head of Revenue Finance
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: MedSentryX — request for flex credit exception (POC → enterprise) — sensitivity & memo draft

Laura / Markus —

Thanks — attached is a short sensitivity table in the same workbook (tab: sensitivity) showing conservative / expected / upside consumption and corresponding gross margin impact. Key notes:
- Conservative: $650k consumption in year 1; expected: $1.1M; upside: $1.8M (if platform gets adopted at 3 sites).
- The $300k cap prevents >40% downside to our year 1 unit economics in the upside case.
- Precedent: Two mid-market healthcare pilots in 2026 where we provided a similar amortized credit with strict consumption caps; both converted and produced >2x ARR within 18 months.

Draft memo (for exec):
---
To: Markus Klein, CFO
From: Priyom Das / Laura Bennett
Re: MedSentryX — request for 28% flex credit on starter slab for first 12 months (cap $300k)
Background: MedSentryX has completed an engineering POC and requires a fiscal start window to complete procurement. Losing the window will likely delay conversion to enterprise until Q4 and push the reference opportunity to a competitor.
Recommendation: Approve the flex credit as a committed, amortized credit capped at $300k. Finance has modeled the sensitivity table and shows an acceptable margin impact at the conservative case.
Risks: Sets a precedent for large starter discounts in healthcare; mitigate by documenting the cap and requiring exec approval for any repeat exceptions within 24 months.
Approval requested: CFO signoff for one-time exception; VP Sales (Marissa) to sign commercial term sheet.
---

If you want I can tighten the memo language and hand it to Markus for brief review.

Priyom

Attachment noted: MedSentryX_MA_plan.xlsx (updated)

From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwoodinference.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2028-04-14T17:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MedSentryX — request for flex credit exception (POC → enterprise) — CFO clearance

Thanks for the package and the sensitivity analysis. I reviewed the numbers with finance. Two quick edits before I sign:
1) Add an explicit clause in the term sheet that the credit is non-transferable and cannot be applied to any subsequent purchase orders beyond the 12-month window.
2) Add a customer-obligation clause requiring MedSentryX to commit to a named pilot-to-production plan (milestones) with two checkpoints — 90 days and 180 days — that trigger retention of the remaining credit. If they miss both checkpoints the remaining credit expires.

With those clauses added I approve the flex credit exception (up to 28% capped at $300k for the first 12 months) and authorize Marissa to sign the commercial term sheet on behalf of Redwood.

Please loop legal to draft the specific language; priory: non-transferability, milestone triggers, and credit amortization schedule.

- Markus Klein
Chief Financial Officer
Redwood Inference
